name: idc-nsclc-radiogenomics
description:
Radiogenomics needs the same patients measured both ways, and almost no public resource provides it. This collection does: 211 patients imaged with thin-section CT and whole-body PET/CT before surgical excision, with a subset carrying matched microarray expression data deposited separately in the Gene Expression Omnibus.
The link between the two is recorded in the collection description as prose, not as a structured cross-reference, which is why the pairing is easy to miss. We extract that accession automatically and surface it here. Everything is openly downloadable with no account.
citeAs: A radiogenomic dataset of non-small cell lung cancer

recordSet.name: Clinical variables with measured completeness
recordSet.description: Completeness is measured from the source repository's own records. A field populated entirely with non-answers is reported as populated but not informative, because it blocks an analysis just as surely as an absent field.

supportedQuestions: Do quantitative CT or PET features predict gene expression programs in lung adenocarcinoma?
How reproducible are radiomic features across CT and PET acquisitions of the same tumor?
Can models trained on this cohort's segmentations generalize to other lung imaging collections in the same repository?

blockingLimitations.statement: The matched imaging-and-expression subset is a small fraction of the 211 imaged patients - the collection describes roughly 26 cases with microarray data. The cohort is imaging-rich and genomics-poor.

inappropriateUses: Training a deep radiogenomic model end to end.
Population-level claims about lung cancer imaging phenotypes.
